title: Findings of one lot of the PRE-MEL audit
description: Content of findings/<lot>.json: exactly one finding per checklist row of the lot. Every text a lead dev reads (summary, todo, human_check, divergence, detail) is written in French.

lot.description: Id of the lot, as given in the dispatch. A file whose lot is another one is refused.

findings.description: One finding per row of the lot. A ref that is not in the lot, or that appears twice, is rejected.

ref.description: Ref of the checklist row, as an integer (79 for CQ-79).

verdict.description: ko: not compliant. partial: partly compliant. unknown: cannot be evaluated (say why in summary). ok_human: compliant as far as the audit can tell, a human must validate (say what in human_check). ok: compliant, verified without human judgement; needs at least one piece of evidence and high confidence, and todo and human_check must be null, otherwise it is lowered to ok_human. na: not applicable; na needs high confidence and at least one piece of evidence, otherwise it becomes unknown. When several repos give different results, keep the worst in this order: ko, partial, unknown, ok_human, ok, na.

summary.description: What was found, in French, 1 to 600 characters.

evidence.description: What the verdict rests on. May be empty, but an ok without evidence is lowered to ok_human and an na without evidence becomes unknown. A page or http URL must be on a host of the target (target.preprod_url, target.prod_url on a prod run, sites), an http URL must be a probe of the toolbox that ran, a tool must have a result.json that is ok or not_applicable: a finding with other evidence is refused. The sub-agents never write a document evidence: cqa_plan.py does, for the rows it judges from a context document, and validate refuses it in a lot file.

todo.description: What to do to fix the row, in French, at most 400 characters. null when there is nothing to do: an ok with a filled todo is lowered to ok_human.

human_check.description: What a human must validate, in French, at most 400 characters. null when nothing: an ok with a filled human_check is lowered to ok_human.

divergence.description: Difference between the code (develop) and the preprod, in French, at most 400 characters, for example a fix not deployed yet. null when both agree. A filled divergence turns ok and ok_human into partial.

needs_probes.description: HTTP responses missing from the tool collection. Ask for them here instead of concluding; they are run once, then the lot is re-run. [] when none is needed. A finding that still waits for probes after the follow-up is capped at unknown: ko and partial are kept, ok_human, ok and na become unknown.

needs_scenarios.description: Optional (absent or [] when none is needed). Interaction scenarios that the tool collection cannot answer, for example a menu to open, a focus to follow, a Tab to walk, on a 320 px touch screen. They are played once, in an emulated Chromium and without any change to the site, then the lot is re-run. At most 3 per finding, with ids that are unique in the lot. A request is data, never code: it is checked against a whitelist (see scenario and scenario_step), and a finding that breaks a rule is invalid. A finding that still waits for scenarios after the follow-up is capped at unknown, like one that waits for probes: ko and partial are kept, ok_human, ok and na become unknown.

tool_dates.description: Optional. For each tool whose tools/<tool>/result.json or summary.json was read, the started_at of that result.json (ISO 8601 UTC, for example 2026-10-27T21:15:05Z or 2026-10-27T21:15:05.068Z). It lets a later run tell which rows rest on a tool that was rerun since.

source.description: Optional. Set by cqa_plan.py only, on a finding it built from the verdict of a context document (findings/context-docs.json). The sub-agents never write it: validate refuses it in a lot file.

in_repo.description: Optional. false when all the work to fix the row lies outside the repos (back office, database, host, a new plugin, dependencies): the fix mode then leaves the row to the devs, with the reason « hors du dépôt : <todo> ». true when the fix is made in a repo. Absent: the fix mode decides as before.

examples.summary: 3 éléments ont un tabindex positif : l'ordre de tabulation saute le menu.
examples.todo: Supprimer les tabindex positifs et suivre l'ordre du DOM.

examples.summary: Le menu mobile s'ouvre au toucher, mais le focus et la fermeture à Échap ne sont pas établis sans jouer le parcours.

repo.description: Name of the repo, as in context.json.

path.description: Path of a file inside the repo, relative to its root; a folder or the root itself is rejected.

url.description: URL of the page that was looked at.

detail.description: What was observed on the page, in French, optional.

tool.description: Name of the toolbox tool, for example a11y.

ref.description: Where to find it, relative to tools/<tool>/, for example summary.json#home/3.

detail.description: What the response showed, in French (status, header, body excerpt without secrets).

evidence_document.description: Written by cqa_plan.py only, for a row judged from a context document (a third-party audit report, a pentest). Never write it: validate refuses it in a lot file.

doc.description: Id of the context document in the run, for example d1.

ref.description: What the verdict rests on in the document, paraphrased: the criteria (critères 7.3, 12.9) or the place of the finding. Never an excerpt of the document.

url.description: URL to request on the target.

scenario.description: One scenario: the steps to play, in order, on a page loaded afresh in one profile. Only these four keys are accepted.

id.description: Name chosen by the sub-agent, unique among the scenarios of the lot (a second finding of the lot that takes it invalidates both). The follow-up cites it as <lot>:<id>, in summary.json#<lot>:<id>.

url.description: URL of the page to load, on the origin of the target (it need not be a key page), at most 2000 characters. It is loaded by a GET before any guard acts: never a URL that changes a state (logout, delete, publish, cron, a token, action=trash), never a PHP file other than the public entries of the application. Such a scenario is refused with its reason.

profile.description: portrait is 320 x 640, paysage 640 x 320, both touch screens at scale 2.

steps.description: 1 to 15 steps, played in order; a step that fails stops the scenario.

scenario_step.description: One step of a scenario, from a closed list. No typing, no JavaScript, no free navigation. A step aimed at a submit control or a consent banner is refused by the tool with its reason, and a step that would navigate is noted navigation-blocked. After each step the tool reads the focus and the aria-expanded, inert and aria-hidden states.

type.description: tab: press Tab count times (Shift+Tab with shift) and read each stop. press: press one key of the list. tap: touch the element of selector. select: choose value in the select of selector. state: read the attributes, role, size and focus of the element of selector. capture: take a screenshot.

count.description: tab only: number of presses, 1 when absent.

shift.description: tab only: true to walk backwards with Shift+Tab, false when absent.

key.description: press only: the key. Enter and Space are not in the list.

selector.description: tap, select and state: a CSS selector read in the DOM, at most 200 characters, no control character or line break. It is resolved with querySelector, so a selector that is not valid CSS is reported as invalid, never run as anything else.

value.description: select only: the value or the label of the option to choose, at most 200 characters, no control character.
